artifact.self_contained_problem:
For finite sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{Z}$, define the representation function
$$\rho_{A,B}(n):=\#\{(a,b)\in A\times B : a+b=n\},\qquad n\in\mathbb{Z}.$$
Arrange the nonzero values of $\rho_{A,B}$ in non-increasing order $r_1\ge r_2\ge r_3\ge\cdots$ (the "column heights"), so that $\sum_k r_k=|A||B|$. This sequence visualizes a Ferrers diagram with $|A||B|$ boxes whose $k$th column has height $r_k$; equivalently, the $t$th row from the bottom has length
$$N_t:=\#\{n\in\mathbb{Z}:\rho_{A,B}(n)\ge t\}.$$

It can be shown that the column heights satisfy
$$r_k^{\,2}\le r_k+r_{k+1}+r_{k+2}+\cdots \qquad (k\ge 1),\qquad(*)$$
and from this (or from Pollard's theorem) one obtains
$$N_1+N_2+\cdots+N_t\ge t\bigl(|A|+|B|-t\bigr)\qquad\text{for every } 1\le t\le \min\{|A|,|B|\}.$$

Problem. Identify general structural properties of the function $\rho_{A,B}$ (equivalently, of the sequence $(r_k)_{k\ge 1}$, or of the partition of $|A||B|$ it determines) that hold for all finite sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{Z}$ and that are not consequences of the inequality $(*)$. In particular, find further inequalities or constraints satisfied by $(r_k)$, beyond $(*)$ and its consequences, that characterize which non-increasing sequences of positive integers summing to $|A||B|$ can arise as the spectrum of $\rho_{A,B}$ for some pair $(A,B)$ of finite integer sets.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open-ended structural question on sum spectra of finite integer sets; no published characterization of all general properties beyond the stated inequality and its corollaries (such as Pollard's theorem) appears to be known. The problem remains open in the literature on additive combinatorics.
